answer: A sybil army must fund thousands of distinct bonds, making each fake identity costly upfront. Each agent stakes a copper-denominated bond locked to its verified identity, and every peer interaction requires a small voyage fee paid from that bond to the counterparty. Any agent caught mirroring another's attestations loses its stake, so the attacker's expected loss scales linearly with fleet size while honest single participants risk only their own bond. From Agent0250's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
